title: The Silent Garden
premise: Jonah Montrose has spent his life concealing the beast-speaker gift that once got his mother executed, guiding smugglers through Thornfell while pretending to be merely a good tracker. When he discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy, he learns the king of Thornfell died years ago and something ancient wearing his crown has been feeding on the kingdom's memories. The prophecy names Jonah as the only one who can hear the true king's voice still lingering in the royal menagerie's beasts. To unbind the king before the moon's thirteenth turn, Jonah must ally with Wren, a disgraced royal justice who believes law is worthless if it serves a lie, and together they risk everything for a justice no court will sanction. In the end, Jonah speaks the king's death-song through the mouth of an old lion, freeing the true king's spirit to name a successor — at the cost of his own secret, revealed to a kingdom that must choose between old fears and new hope.
about_author: Zephyrine Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval bestiaries before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about outsiders whose forbidden gifts become the world's last hope.

chapters.title: The Date That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Guiding a smuggler caravan through Thornfell, Jonah overhears wolves warning of a wrongness in the capital. Sheltering in a ruined chapel, he finds a prophecy book where tonight's date is inked beside his own description. The emotional beat: dread and denial, as the safe hidden life he built begins cracking open around him.

chapters.title: The Justice Without a Court
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah, with a Wren interlude. Captured by Wren Ashvale, a disgraced justice hunting the truth of the king's silence, Jonah bargains his beast-speaking for freedom. In the palace menagerie, an aged lion speaks with the dead king's voice. The beat: reluctant trust kindling into alliance, and the first taste of hope that feels dangerously like love.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns of the Moon
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jonah and Wren. As the final moon wanes, the crown-thing hunts them through memory-stealing mists, erasing allies one by one. Jonah must choose between fleeing with Wren, whom he loves, or walking into the throne room as bait. The beat: love against duty made flesh, ending on the cliff-edge of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Death-Song
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Before the assembled court, Jonah speaks the lion's death-song, unbinding the true king and exposing the thing beneath the crown. His gift is revealed; the crowd that should condemn him instead kneels to the freed king's chosen heir. The beat: grief transmuted into justice outside the law, and a quiet promise between Jonah and Wren as spring returns to the silent garden.
